- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.10) over recent days, model tends to under-forecast; increase forecast slightly to align with bullish momentum.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.30), model often over-forecasts; reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% to reflect bearish bias.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days); apply a “cool-down” correction: subtract 1–2% from forecast 2–3 days post-spike.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive forecasts are above 70.00, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% per day to avoid overbought trap.
- For 30-day horizon, model underestimates true price in 70–75% of cases when sentiment is neutral or mildly bullish — adjust upward by 0.8–1.2% if sentiment > 0.05.
- Lagged sentiment effect: if sentiment was positive 3–5 days ago, model often misses the momentum; add 0.3–0.7% to forecast to capture delayed reaction.
